result:
The recon is written: four files under `recon/` plus the filled-in `env.md`, with file and offset evidence for each claim. Nothing under `games/` changed and neither game was run. **Main result: Portal is fine to mod, but the TABG side is blocked by Easy Anti-Cheat, even on community servers.**

**The blocker:**
- `TABG_Launcher.exe` is Epic's anti-cheat launcher under another name (its version info says "Easy Anti-Cheat Bootstrapper (EOS)").
- On every server join, the game itself starts an anti-cheat session and disconnects if that fails (`Landfall/Easy_AC_Client.cs`). This happens on official, community and self-hosted servers alike, and TABG has no offline mode.
- So "community servers only" still means a protected game process. Loading BepInEx into it is the framework's anti-cheat stop sign. Running the game without anti-cheat would be bypassing it, so I ruled out every way of doing that. One of them is a developer switch in Epic's SDK; I noted it only so nobody later assumes it's acceptable.

**You need to pick a direction** (`MODDING_PLAN.md` §3):
- **A:** Ask Landfall whether there is, or will be, an approved anti-cheat-free mode for community servers. This is my recommendation as the first step.
- **B:** Swap the host to an unprotected Unity game. TABS (Totally Accurate Battle Simulator) is the natural fit, but it isn't installed or checked.
- **C:** A separate overlay window on top of TABG. It never touches the game, but it can't hide Portal behind TABG objects and doesn't follow TABG's camera.
- **D:** Pause the TABG side.

Slices 2–4 (link, Portal frame export, fakehost) don't need TABG and can go ahead now.

**Other findings:**
- **Engines:** TABG is Unity 2021.3.45f2, Mono, 64-bit. BepInEx 5.4.23.5 win_x64 matches it if the block lifts. Portal is Valve's late-2024 single-player rebuild, all 32-bit, with no anti-cheat.
- **Physics:** TABG uses Unity's standard physics with ragdoll characters, not its own solver. Invisible colliders will stop characters and can act as floor, and characters can be flung. Collision layer 29 "OnlyLocalPlayer" affects only your own character, which is ideal for the chamber.
- **Networking:** TABG uses separate dedicated servers. Addresses come from official matchmaking, Landfall's community server list, direct IP (default port 7777), or a relay join code.
- **Design conflict:** each player's game reports its own position to the server. Standing in the chamber, being flung or warping through a portal would all be visible to the server and other players. Only the pure visual overlay stays client-side.
- **Portal hookup:** a replacement `client.dll` isn't possible, because Portal's own game code isn't in the Source SDK. The working route is a server plugin (`portal/addons/*.vdf`) built against the Source SDK 2013 headers; its interface versions match this build. The engine has the depth targets and shaders needed for frame and depth export.

**Corrections to the existing docs** (applied in `env.md`):
- The game is Totally Accurate Battlegrounds (Steam appid 823130), not "Tag: The Game".
- The game folders are `games/Portal/` and `games/TotallyAccurateBattlegrounds/`, not `games/portal/` and `games/tabg/`.
- One Source unit is 2.54 cm according to the engine's own physics constants, not 1.17 cm.

**Method notes:**
- `pip install --user ./universal-modder` worked (`uv` isn't on this box), and `um scan` ran on both games. Its "ASI loader" result for Portal is wrong: those two files are sound-codec plugins.
- I installed .NET 8 and `ilspycmd` 9.1 user-locally; the newest `ilspycmd` won't install on .NET 8.
- The decompiled TABG code is in `/tmp/tabg_decomp/`, outside the project and not committed, so it will disappear on reboot.
